name: Bulleh Shah
birth_place: Disputed: Uch Gillanian/Bahawalpur region or Pandoke/Qasur region, Punjab
languages: Arabic and Persian learning reported/inferred from poetry and later accounts
short_bio: Bulleh Shah is the conventional name of an eighteenth-century Punjabi Sufi poet, usually identified as Abdullah Shah and dated approximately 1680 to 1757 or 1758. Later sources associate him with Kasur, education in Arabic and Persian, and discipleship under the Lahore-based spiritual teacher Shah Inayat Qadiri. The surviving biography is largely reconstructed from later hagiography and the poems themselves; birthplace, exact dates, education details, anecdotes, and even the boundaries of the attributed corpus remain disputed. His verse is strongly tied to performance and uses Punjabi folk and romance imagery, especially Heer-Ranjha, to explore love, selfhood, religious identity, and social hierarchy.
